verses.text: Paul, an apostle (sent one). I was not sent from men, neither by man. I was sent by Jesus Christ and by God the Father. God the Father raised Jesus from the dead.
And all the brothers who are with me write with me to the churches of Galatia:
Grace be to you, and peace, from God the Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.
Jesus gave Himself for our sins. He did this to deliver (rescue) us from this present evil world. This was the will of God and our Father.
To God be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I marvel (am amazed) at you. You are so soon removed (turned away) from God, who called you into the grace of Christ. You have turned to another gospel (good news).
But it is not another gospel (good news). There are some who trouble you. They want to pervert (twist) the gospel (good news) of Christ.
Suppose we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel (good news) to you. Suppose it is different from what we have preached to you. Then let that one be accursed (punished by God).
As we said before, so I say now again. Suppose anyone preaches to you any other gospel (good news) than what you received. Then let that person be accursed (punished by God).
Do I now persuade (try to win over) people, or God? Do I seek to please people? If I still pleased people, I would not be the servant of Christ.
Brothers, I certify (make known to) you that the gospel (good news) I preached is not after man (from people).
I did not receive it from man. Neither was I taught it. It came by the revelation (showing) of Jesus Christ.
You have heard of my conversation (way of life) in time past in the Jews' religion. Beyond measure I persecuted (attacked for faith) the church of God. I wasted (destroyed) it.
I profited (went ahead) in the Jews' religion above many my equals (of my own age) in my nation. I was much more zealous (eager) for the traditions of my fathers.
But it pleased God, who separated (set) me apart from my mother's womb. God called me by His grace.

It pleased God to reveal (show) His Son in me. God did this so that I might preach the Son among the heathen (people who are not Jews). Immediately I did not confer (talk it over) with flesh and blood (any human).
Neither did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles (sent ones) before me. I went into Arabia, and returned again to Damascus.
Then after 3 years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter. I abode (stayed) with Peter 15 days.
But of the other apostles (sent ones) I saw none, except James the Lord's brother.
Look, before God, I do not lie about the things which I write to you.
Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
The churches of Judaea which were in Christ did not know my face.
They had only heard this: The man who persecuted (attacked for faith) us in times past now preaches the faith. That man once destroyed that faith.
And they glorified (praised) God in me.

verses.text: Then 14 years after, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas. I took Titus with me also.

I went up by revelation (showing). I communicated (explained) to them the gospel (good news) which I preach among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). I did this privately to those who were of reputation (well-known leaders). I did this so that I would not run, or have run, in vain (for nothing).
Titus, who was with me, was a Greek. Yet Titus was not compelled (forced) to be circumcised.

This was because of false brothers unawares brought in (sneaked in). They came in privily (secretly) to spy out our liberty (freedom) which we have in Christ Jesus. They wanted to bring us into bondage (slavery).
We did not give place (give in) to them by subjection (obeying them), no, not for an hour. We did this so that the truth of the gospel (good news) might continue with you.

Some leaders seemed to be somewhat (important). Whatever they were, it makes no matter to me. God accepts no man's person (does not favor anyone). Those who seemed to be somewhat (important) added nothing to me in conference (talking with me).

They saw that the gospel (good news) of the uncircumcision (people who are not circumcised) was committed (trusted) to me. The gospel (good news) of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews) was committed (trusted) to Peter.

God worked effectually (powerfully) in Peter for the apostleship (being a sent one) of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews). The same God was mighty in me toward the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).

James, Peter, and John seemed to be pillars. They perceived (saw) the grace that was given to me. So they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship (sharing). We would go to the heathen (people who are not Jews). They would go to the circumcision (the circumcised Jews).
They only wanted us to remember the poor. I also was forward (eager) to do that same thing.
But Peter came to Antioch. Then I withstood (stood against) Peter to his face, because he was to be blamed.

Before certain men came from James, Peter ate with the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). But when those men had come, Peter withdrew and separated himself. Peter feared those who were of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews).
And the other Jews dissembled (pretended) along with Peter. Even Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation (pretending).

But I saw that they did not walk uprightly. They did not walk according to the truth of the gospel (good news). So I said to Peter before them all: You are a Jew, but you live after the manner of Gentiles (people who are not Jews). You do not live as the Jews do. So why do you compel (force) the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) to live as the Jews do?
We are Jews by nature (birth), and not sinners of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).

We know that a person is not justified (made right with God) by the works of the law. A person is justified (made right with God) by the faith of Jesus Christ. So we also have believed in Jesus Christ. We did this to be justified (made right with God) by the faith of Christ. We are not justified (made right with God) by the works of the law. For by the works of the law no flesh (person) will be justified (made right with God).
But we seek to be justified (made right with God) by Christ. Suppose we ourselves are also found sinners. Is Christ then the minister (servant) of sin? God forbid.
If I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor (lawbreaker).
For I through the law am dead to the law. This is so that I might live to God.
I am crucified with Christ. Nevertheless I live, yet not I, but Christ lives in me. I now live in the flesh (body) by the faith of the Son of God. The Son of God loved me, and gave Himself for me.
I do not frustrate (throw away) the grace of God. If righteousness (being right with God) comes by the law, then Christ is dead in vain (died for nothing).

verses.text: O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched (put a spell on) you, that you should not obey the truth? Jesus Christ has been evidently (clearly) set forth before your eyes, crucified among you.
I want to learn only this from you. Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law? Or did you receive the Spirit by the hearing of faith?
Are you so foolish? You began in the Spirit. Are you now made perfect (complete) by the flesh (sinful self)?
Have you suffered so many things in vain (for nothing)? If it is yet in vain (for nothing).
God ministers (gives) the Spirit to you, and works miracles among you. Does God do it by the works of the law? Or does God do it by the hearing of faith?
It is just as with Abraham. Abraham believed God, and it was accounted (counted) to him for righteousness (being right with God).
So know that those who are of faith are the children of Abraham.

The scripture foresaw (saw ahead of time) that God would justify (make right with God) the heathen (people who are not Jews) through faith. So the scripture preached the gospel (good news) before to Abraham. It said: In you will all nations be blessed.
So then those who are of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

As many as are of the works of the law are under the curse (God's punishment). For it is written: Cursed (punished by God) is everyone who does not continue (keep on) doing all things written in the book of the law.
No one is justified (made right with God) by the law in the sight of God. That is evident (clear). For: The just (those who are right with God) will live by faith.
And the law is not of faith. But: The one who does them will live in them.

Christ has redeemed (bought back and set free) us from the curse (God's punishment) of the law. Christ was made a curse (took God's punishment) for us. For it is written: Cursed (punished by God) is everyone who hangs on a tree.

Christ did this so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). It comes through Jesus Christ. Christ also did this so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
Brothers, I speak after the manner of men (in an everyday way). It may be only a man's covenant (agreement). Yet if it is confirmed, no one disannuls (cancels) it, or adds to it.
Now the promises were made to Abraham and his seed. God does not say: And to seeds, as of many. But God says it as of one: And to your seed, which is Christ.

And this I say. God confirmed the covenant (agreement) before, in Christ. The law came 430 years after. The law cannot disannul (cancel) that covenant (agreement). The law cannot make the promise of no effect (worthless).
If the inheritance is of the law, it is no more of promise. But God gave it to Abraham by promise.

Why then does the law serve? It was added because of transgressions (lawbreaking). It was added till the Seed should come to whom the promise was made. And the law was ordained (set in order) by angels in the hand of a mediator (go-between).
Now a mediator (go-between) is not a mediator (go-between) of one. But God is one.
Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid. Suppose a law had been given which could have given life. Then truly righteousness (being right with God) would have been by the law.
But the scripture has concluded (shut up) all under sin. This was so that the promise might be given to those who believe. The promise comes by faith of Jesus Christ.
But before faith came, we were kept under the law. We were shut up to the faith which should afterwards be revealed (shown).
So the law was our schoolmaster (guardian) to bring us to Christ. This was so that we might be justified (made right with God) by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster (guardian).
For you are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.
As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is neither Jew nor Greek. There is neither bond (slave) nor free. There is neither male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed. You are heirs according to the promise.

verses.text: Now I say this. As long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a servant. This is so even though he is lord (owner) of all.
But the heir is under tutors (guardians) and governors (managers). This lasts until the time appointed (set) by the father.
It is the same with us. When we were children, we were in bondage (slavery) under the elements (basic rules) of the world.
But the fulness of the time came. Then God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
To redeem (buy back and set free) those who were under the law. God did this so that we might receive the adoption (being made God's children) of sons.
And you are sons. So God has sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts. The Spirit cries: Abba (Daddy), Father.
So you are no more a servant, but a son. And if you are a son, then you are an heir of God through Christ.
But back then you did not know God. Then you did service (were slaves) to those which by nature are no gods.
But now you have known God, or rather are known by God. So how do you turn again to the weak and beggarly (poor) elements (basic rules)? Do you desire again to be in bondage (slavery) to them?
You observe (keep) days, and months, and times, and years.
I am afraid for you. I fear I have bestowed (spent) labour (hard work) on you in vain (for nothing).
Brothers, I beseech (beg) you, be as I am, for I am as you are. You have not injured me at all.
You know how I preached the gospel (good news) to you at the first. It was through infirmity (weakness) of the flesh (body).
My temptation (trial) was in my flesh (body). But you did not despise (look down on) it, nor reject it. You received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
Where is then the blessedness (happiness) you spoke of? I bear you record (tell you truly) of this. If it had been possible, you would have plucked out your own eyes. You would have given them to me.
Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
They zealously affect (eagerly seek after) you, but not well. Yes, they would exclude (shut out) you. They want you to affect (eagerly seek after) them.
But it is good to be zealously affected (eagerly sought after) always in a good thing. It should not be only when I am present with you.
My little children, I travail (have birth pains) in birth for you again. I will do so until Christ is formed in you.
I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice (speak to you in a different way). For I stand in doubt of (am unsure about) you.
Tell me, you who desire to be under the law: Do you not hear the law?
For it is written that Abraham had 2 sons. One son was by a bondmaid (slave woman). The other son was by a freewoman.
But the son of the bondwoman (slave woman) was born after the flesh (in the natural way). But the son of the freewoman was by promise.

These things are an allegory (a story with a deeper meaning). For these are the 2 covenants (agreements). One covenant (agreement) is from the mount Sinai, which gives birth to bondage (slavery). This one is Agar (Hagar).
For this Agar (Hagar) is mount Sinai in Arabia. She answers to (stands for) Jerusalem which now is. Jerusalem is in bondage (slavery) with her children.
But Jerusalem which is above is free. She is the mother of us all.

For it is written: Rejoice, you barren (woman who cannot have children) who does not bear. Break forth and cry, you who do not travail (have birth pains). For the desolate (lonely woman) has many more children than she who has a husband.
Now we, brothers, as Isaac was, are the children of promise.
Back then, the son born after the flesh (in the natural way) persecuted (attacked for faith) the son born after the Spirit. Even so it is now.
Nevertheless what does the scripture say? Cast out the bondwoman (slave woman) and her son. For the son of the bondwoman (slave woman) will not be heir with the son of the freewoman.
So then, brothers, we are not children of the bondwoman (slave woman), but of the free.

verses.text: Stand fast therefore in the liberty (freedom) with which Christ has made us free. Do not be entangled again with the yoke (wooden bar for working together) of bondage (slavery).
Look, I Paul say to you: If you are circumcised, Christ will profit (help) you nothing.
For I testify again to every man who is circumcised. That man is a debtor (bound) to do the whole law.
Christ has become of no effect (no help) to whoever of you are justified (made right with God) by the law. You have fallen from grace.
For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness (being right with God) by faith.
For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision avails (counts for) anything, nor uncircumcision. What counts is faith which works by love.
You did run well. Who did hinder (stop) you, so that you should not obey the truth?
This persuasion (way of thinking) does not come from God, who calls you.
A little leaven (yeast) leavens the whole lump (makes the whole batch of dough rise).
I have confidence in you through the Lord. I trust that you will be no otherwise minded (think no other way). But whoever troubles you will bear their judgment, whoever they are.
And I, brothers, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution (being attacked for faith)? Then the offence (stumbling block) of the cross has ceased (stopped).
I wish that those who trouble you were even cut off.
For, brothers, you have been called to liberty (freedom). Only do not use liberty (freedom) for an occasion (excuse) to the flesh (sinful self). But by love serve one another.
For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this: You will love your neighbour as yourself.
But if you bite and devour (eat up) one another, take heed (be careful). You may be consumed (destroyed) by one another.
This I say then: Walk in the Spirit, and you will not fulfil the lust (wrong desire) of the flesh (sinful self).

For the flesh (sinful self) lusts (has wrong desires) against the Spirit. And the Spirit is against the flesh (sinful self). These are contrary (opposed) to one another. So you cannot do the things that you would.
But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.

Now the works of the flesh (sinful self) are manifest (plain to see). They are these: Adultery (being unfaithful in marriage), fornication (sexual sin), uncleanness (impure living), lasciviousness (shameless sexual desire),

Idolatry (worshipping idols), witchcraft, hatred, variance (fighting), emulations (jealous rivalry), wrath (anger), strife (quarrels), seditions (splitting into sides), heresies (false teaching groups),

Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings (wild parties), and such like. I tell you about these before, as I have also told you in time past. Those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering (patience), gentleness, goodness, faith,
Meekness (being gentle), temperance (self-control). Against such there is no law.
And those who are Christ's have crucified the flesh (sinful self) with the affections (passions) and lusts (wrong desires).
If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
Let us not be desirous of vain glory (empty pride). Let us not provoke one another, or envy one another.

verses.text: Brothers, someone may be overtaken (caught) in a fault. Then you who are spiritual, restore such a one in the spirit of meekness (gentleness). Consider yourself, or you also may be tempted.
Bear (carry) one another's burdens (heavy loads), and so fulfil the law of Christ.
If anyone thinks themselves to be something, when they are nothing, they deceive (fool) themselves.
But let everyone prove (test) their own work. Then they will have rejoicing in themselves alone, and not in another.
For everyone will bear (carry) their own burden (load).
Let the one who is taught in the word communicate (share) with the teacher. Let them share in all good things.
Do not be deceived (fooled). God is not mocked (made fun of). For whatever a person sows (plants), they will also reap (harvest) that.

Whoever sows (plants) to their flesh (sinful self) will reap (harvest) corruption (decay) from the flesh (sinful self). But whoever sows (plants) to the Spirit will reap (harvest) life everlasting from the Spirit.
And let us not be weary in well doing (doing good). For in due season (at the right time) we will reap (harvest), if we do not faint (lose heart).
So as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people. Let us do good especially to those who are of the household (family) of faith.
You see how large a letter I have written to you with my own hand.

Some desire to make a fair show (look good) in the flesh (on the outside). They constrain (force) you to be circumcised. They do it only so that they will not suffer persecution (being attacked for faith) for the cross of Christ.
Those who are circumcised do not keep the law themselves. But they desire to have you circumcised. Then they may glory (brag) in your flesh (body).
But God forbid that I should glory (brag) in anything. I glory (brag) only in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ. By Christ the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails (counts for) anything, nor uncircumcision. What counts is a new creature (creation).
Peace be on as many as walk according to this rule. Mercy be on them, and on the Israel of God.
From now on let no one trouble me. For I bear (carry) in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.
Brothers, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
